162-b-a-minor-concentrations: Programs marked ** are in other faculties. Music minors (Composition, Education, History, Science and Technology, Theory, Applications of Technology) are under Arts or Schulich. Management for Non-Management Students is under Desautels. Also: Quebec Studies and Community-Engaged Learning (18 credits).
180-group-d: Another 3 credits may come from Group A or B. The rest from COMP 230 and COMP at 300+, not COMP 396.
180-program-description: Techniques and methods for designing complex software systems. Can combine with the Supplementary Minor in Computer Science. Doesn't lead to Professional Engineer certification.
Finish MATH 133, 140, 141 or equivalents first. Two programs in one unit means a third elsewhere is needed to graduate.
180-required-courses-30-credits: With programming knowledge, swap COMP 202 for a complementary.
180-complementary-courses-6-credits: At least 6 credits from the list or COMP at 300+, not COMP 396. Suggested courses are listed.
181-about-east-asian-studies: Languages and cultures of China, Japan and Korea, from Buddhist art and anime to Korean cinema and Chinese sci-fi, with surveys and seminars on media, gender, religion, archaeology and critical theory.
Small intensive language classes and support for study abroad. M.A. and Ph.D. available. Graduates work in business, academia, law, the arts and sciences.
181-east-asian-language: 9 credits: pass first-level Korean, Chinese or Japanese with C or better. With prior knowledge, do second level, or 6 credits at 400+ plus 3 EAST credits. Placement tests apply.
184-program-description: Advanced study (300+) of an East Asian language you already have, including classical. Can't expand to the Major.
184-complementary-courses-18-credits: Two options: 18 credits of second to fourth level in one language, or advanced language plus 300+ culture, literature or society courses, chosen with the Adviser.
184-program-description-2: Humanities of East Asia: language, society, literature, history, media, religion, politics and art, with core surveys on China, Japan and Korea.
188-program-description: The same training, with surveys leading to individualized seminars. Half your work is here, and half in another Arts program.
190-about-economics: U0 students should take ECON 208 and 209; they're good preparation, though not prerequisites. Don't take ECON 250D or 230D in U0.
Honours is open to B.A. and B.Com. students, who must see an honours adviser every year. Check transfer credit on the Undergraduate Courses page, and consider the Economics Internship Course.
190-standing-in-honours-and-joint-honour: Normally 3.00 program GPA and CGPA for Honours, 3.50 for First-Class. B.Com. Honours and Joint Honours with Finance or Accounting have further rules, including B- in all Management courses.
190-minor-in-management: Economics students can take Desautels' 18-credit Minor for non-Management students (p. 902).
190-location: Leacock Building, 4th Floor, 855 Sherbrooke St. W.
190-program-description: Moderate specialization alongside another major or honours, with the option to switch to or add the Major. There's a special Minor for Management students.
190-complementary-courses-18-credits: 6 from Group A and 12 from Group B.
190-group-b: ECON above 208 (not ECON 295), at least 6 at 300–500.
Only one of ECON 208, 230D or 250D counts; only one of ECON 209, ECON 332 + 333, or ECON 353 + 354. ECON 230D with ECON 209 is allowed.
191-special-minor-in-economics-for-manag: See Desautels' site, and advisers in both units.
191-program-description: A planned 36-credit sequence, normally at McGill. See a majors adviser every year, and attend the August orientation first if you're new. U1 entrants in September go straight to ECON 230D without ECON 208 and 209.

High school math mastery is needed. 200-level usually has no prerequisites; 300–400 needs ECON 230D or 250D, or ECON 208 + 209, or MGCR 293 + ECON 295; 400 also needs Calculus 1 or math techniques. Moving to Honours means meeting all its requirements.
191-required-courses-18-credits: Includes 6 credits of approved statistics; see the Department's rules on statistics.
191-complementary-courses-18-credits: ECON 200-level above 209, and 300–500, with at least 6 at 400–500 and no more than 6 at 200.
191-program-description-2: 30 credits of Honours courses plus 12 approved. Continuing needs B- in ECON 250D and a B- average in Honours courses; otherwise switch out, or you can't graduate with Honours.
Honours: 3.00 GPA in core, 3.00 average in Economics, 3.00 CGPA. First Class: 3.50 in each. Supplemental and original grades both count. See an Honours adviser.
192-required-core-courses-30-credits: Equivalent statistics may waive ECON 257D, normally with ECON 469 added to ECON 468. See the statistics rules.
Usual order: ECON 250D in U1, ECON 353 and 354 in U2, ECON 450 and 452 in U3, ECON 257D in U1 or U2, ECON 468 in U2 or U3.
192-complementary-courses-12-credits: 300–500 approved by an adviser, at least 9 at 400–500 unless approved, usually in U2 or U3. No majors or general courses where an Honours or more advanced course exists.
192-program-description: Combine with another approved discipline, and see an adviser in each department every year.

Same continuation rule as Honours: B- in ECON 250D and a B- average. Graduation: 3.00 GPA in required courses, average and CGPA (3.50 for First Class), both exam grades counted, plus the other component's rules.
193-required-courses-27-credits: Equivalent statistics may waive ECON 257D, normally with ECON 469 added.
193-program-description: Joint with Desautels: 30 Honours economics credits and 30 accounting. See advisers on both sides.
Same continuation and graduation rules for Economics, and B- or better in all Accounting courses, plus Management's Honours rules.
194-economics-required-courses-27-credit: Equivalent statistics may waive ECON 257D, normally with ECON 469 added.
Half of ECON 250D replaces MGCR 293 in the Management Core; half of ECON 257D replaces MGCR 271; half of ECON 353 + 354 replaces ECON 295.
195-program-description: Joint with Desautels: 30 Honours economics credits and 30 finance. Enter with two terms of Calculus. See advisers on both sides.
Same continuation and graduation rules for Economics, and B- or better in all Finance courses, plus Management's Honours rules.
195-economics: Equivalent statistics may waive ECON 257D, normally with ECON 469 added.
195-finance: Half of ECON 250D replaces MGCR 293 in the Core; half of ECON 257D replaces MGCR 271; half of ECON 353 + 354 replaces ECON 295.
197-about-education-for-arts-students: Philosophy and psychology of education, with wider views on theory, practice and current issues. Read the Faculty of Education's procedures before applying. It doesn't qualify you to teach in Québec; see p. 684 for teaching programs.
197-location: Internships and Student Affairs Office, Faculty of Education, 3700 McTavish St.
197-program-description: A footing in pedagogy and possibly a start toward a B.Ed., but no teaching qualification. Limited places, so you must apply; procedures and deadlines are on the Faculty's site. Check Arts rules on outside courses.
198-about-educational-psychology: Learning, cognition and instruction at all ages, technology as a tool for thinking, evaluating and improving teaching, inclusive education, development, family and community, machine learning and learning analytics. See p. 697.
198-program-director: Professor Alenoush Saroyan, 3700 McTavish St., Room 614.
198-program-description: No teaching qualification. With the Psychology Major, you need another Arts minor outside Psychology to meet the Multi-Track rule. Check Arts rules on outside courses.
198-required-course-3-credits: Needs an introductory psychology course from CEGEP or university. Without one, take PSYC 100 or EDPE 300; EDPE 300 can count as a complementary.
198-complementary-courses-15-credits: 3 credits near the end of the program (usually EDPE 355 with a psychology background), then 12 from the list.
Not both EDPE 208 and PSYC 304; EDPE 208 isn't open to Psychology students.
